1) Can Redwood smooth our initial 12-month commitment so the fee bands don't spike in Q1? Finance wants a flat-ish billing profile rather than big step-ups tied to usage bands.
2) We need the invoice split between Acme HealthTech (core org) and Acme Labs (R&D) — same contract, two bill-to entities.

Hi Alyssa / Devon,

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. We've sketched two pragmatic approaches and attached a redline for the pricing exhibit to illustrate both options:

Option A — "Smoothing" (annuitized):
- Convert tiered usage bands into an annualized band with monthly billing at a blended unit rate.
- Maintains the same total expected revenue over the 12-month term but reduces month-to-month volatility.
- We keep the existing minimum commit but waive the quarterly true-up for the first 90 days.

Option B — "Split bill" (labs add-on):
- Primary contract retained by Acme HealthTech; Acme Labs added as a bill-to with a $3k/month admin surcharge to cover cross-org reconciliation.
- Labs usage counts toward aggregate banding so discounts apply holistically.

Key tradeoffs (callouts in redline):
- Smoothing reduces month spikes but increases exposure if usage materially exceeds forecasts; we model a 5% buffer above forecast which shows the financial impact.
- Split-bill requires dual invoicing terms; we proposed the admin surcharge instead of increasing the effective unit price.

I've attached "pricing_exhibit_redline_v1.docx" and a sample revised OrderForm_Acme_v3.pdf. Marissa / Karthik — tagging you for legal/proc comments on the floor/cap language and whether the 90-day true-up is acceptable.

If that looks directionally right, we can lock numbers and push a DocuSign packet. Happy to jump on a quick 20-minute call tomorrow to walk through the redline.

—

All — I reviewed the redline. Commercially fine to approve the smoothing concession with these legal guardrails:

1) 90-day true-up window (as suggested) — after 90 days we revert to standard quarterly true-up.
2) Add a maximum overage cap of 40% above forecast for the first 6 months; charges beyond that revert to standard overage rates to protect revenue.
3) Dual bill-to accepted only as an administrative arrangement; confirm Acme signs the same master agreement and provides a PO/ billing contact per entity. We will not create a separate contract for Labs.

If Naomi is good with those callouts, go ahead and send the attached OrderForm_Acme_v3.pdf with the redline embedded and the DocuSign link. I recommend we show both options in the packet but pre-select the smoothing path.
